findings.summary: The table row "One yield only" is a rule placed inside the sync-vs-async comparison table and the closing remark, so it reads as a stray row.
findings.evidence:
One yield only
Use one yield per dependency: one setup, one value, one teardown.
findings.fix: Move "One yield only" out of the def/async table into its own bullet in section 1, and keep the closing remark as the single statement.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: the exception re-raise and the rollback pattern.
findings.evidence:
Handler exceptions are re-raised at the yield
except there to rollback, then raise
findings.fix: Keep the re-raise as one bullet. Show the rollback as a short code snippet with try/except/raise around the yield.

findings.summary: The teardown-order diagram shows the nodes without saying which dependency is the parent, and the page has no explicit code or example for the order.
findings.evidence:
a up
setup
b up
setup
b down
teardown first
a down
teardown last
findings.fix: Label the diagram with the tree, for example "endpoint needs b, b needs a", so a reader can tell why a sets up first.

findings.summary: The scope table and the ordering diagram are separate, and the "App, Router, Route, Parameters" order is shown as bare unlabeled nodes.
findings.fix: Add a caption such as "Execution order, outermost first" above the diagram.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: the Depends() shorthand and the benefit of a class over a dict.
findings.evidence: Wins over a dict for typed attributes (p.skip) and editor autocomplete
findings.fix: Move the class-versus-dict comparison to a separate labelled bullet, or to the interview point only, to avoid repeating it.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: what the override map does and what the lambda example shows.
findings.evidence: Fake's own params resolve as usual: lambda: User(id=1) skips auth
findings.fix: Split into "The fake's own params resolve as usual" and "Example: lambda: User(id=1) skips auth".

findings.summary: The Check yourself page leaves a term inconsistent with earlier pages: it says "user and admin" while the chain on page 2 is get_current_user and require_admin.
findings.evidence: get_db is used by both user and admin, and the route declares only admin.
findings.fix: Use the page 2 names: get_db used by both get_current_user and require_admin, and the route declares only require_admin.
